subject: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output requirements
thread_summary: Post-discovery recap covering Finova's requirements for tool/function calling and deterministic structured JSON output. Agreed success criteria, next steps (test harness, engineering deep-dive, SOC2), and tentative POC timeline.
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@finova.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output requirements

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the specific requirements you called out so we’re all aligned: 

1) Primary pain points
- Inconsistent extraction: current LLM responses vary in field names and formatting, causing downstream parsing failures.
- Hallucinated values for merchant metadata and risk flags.
- Hard to enforce deterministic outputs for downstream processing (payments reconciliation, fraud rules).

2) Current stack
- Finova runs a Node-based orchestration layer that calls an internal model for NLU, then runs business logic and persisting to Postgres.
- You have a lightweight tool-calling pattern today (HTTP webhooks for enrichment), but want tighter agent workflows and schema guarantees before you expand to production.

3) Success criteria (what you said matters)
- Strict JSON-only output matching a pre-defined schema (no surrounding prose, no markdown fences).
- Validation pass rate >= 98% on production-like payloads during POC.
- Clear error-object behavior when the model cannot satisfy schema (standardized error_code + human-readable message).
- Deterministic field ordering is nice-to-have for diffs but not mandatory as long as schema validation is reliable.
- Data residency: all inference must stay in US regions.

4) Tool/function-calling & agent workflow notes
- Proposed workflow: 1) Agent extracts raw entities -> 2) Model executes deterministic formatter/tool layer -> 3) Validator checks JSON schema -> 4) On success call internal webhook to persist / on failure return error object and mark for manual review.
- We discussed the need for a JSON schema you can run locally as the single source of truth for validation. Attached is the draft schema we sketched during the call (finova_payment_schema_v1.json).

Example of required output (single-line JSON; model must NOT include commentary):
{
  "transaction_id": "string",
  "customer_id": "string",
  "amount": "number",
  "currency": "string",
  "merchant": "string",
  "timestamp": "ISO8601",
  "status": "string",
  "risk_flags": ["string"]
}

Deterministic formatting success criteria we propose:
- Output must be valid JSON parseable by standard parsers.
- No leading/trailing text outside the JSON object.
- If the model cannot fully populate required fields, it must return a defined error object: {"error_code":"SCHEMA_MISMATCH", "error_message":"..."}.
- Tool-calling should be auditable: each call returns a stable call_id and status.

5) Next steps (agreed)
- I’ll send the POC proposal and a small test harness you can run internally against your sample payloads (we’ll include a Dockerized validator and a small harness that simulates agent tool calls).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your engineering team (suggested: next Wed 10:00am PDT).
- We’ll surface SOC2 / security docs and RA for data residency.

Attachments: finova_payment_schema_v1.json (draft schema), example test plan link in the Drive.

If I missed anything or you want different acceptance criteria, tell me and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll send the POC doc + test harness by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — talk soon.

Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

--
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference for engineering teams

From: Elena Morales <elena@finova.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Turner <sam.turner@finova.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output requirements

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear recap, this aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

- Please add "currency" as a required field in the schema (we process USD + EUR initially).
- Our target for the POC is 98%+ valid outputs matching schema on a 1k-message sample drawn from our backlog.
- Data residency: must be US-only for PII-sensitive payloads; non-PII can run in EU later.
- We’ll need SOC2 Type II evidence before any prod contract; please include the latest report and your DPA template.
- Can you include a simple pricing sketch for a 30-day POC and for a 6-month pilot with reserved capacity?

We attached a small set of sample payloads (sample_payloads.csv) you can use for the initial validation run.

I’m fine with the engineering deep-dive next Wed (10am PDT) — I’ll invite our infra lead (Sam). Any materials you can circulate before that call (POC scope + test harness readme) would be great.

Best,
Elena
Head of Payments Product | Finova
elena@finova.com
